title: North America
subtitle: North America, 1492–1900
bordersNote: Crisp: US states & territories (Newberry AHCB), colonies and republics (OpenHistoricalMap), each nation's land until its cession to the US (Royce 1899, USFS 2018). Soft: snapshot claims and Indigenous homelands (historical-basemaps, GPL; approximate). Paper claims are weaker than held land, so overlaps read as frontier or contested.

card.name: The Colonisation of North America
card.significance: Four centuries of contact, conquest and dispossession: Spanish, French, British, Dutch and Russian empires amid hundreds of Native nations, and the rise of the United States, Canada and Mexico across a continent.

chapters.title: Contact and conquest
chapters.blurb: Columbus to Jamestown: Spanish conquest of Mexico and the Caribbean, early French and English voyages.

chapters.title: Colonial empires
chapters.blurb: Jamestown, Quebec and New Amsterdam; English, French, Dutch and Spanish colonies amid Native nations.

chapters.title: Seven Years' War
chapters.blurb: The French and Indian War; France leaves the mainland in the Treaty of Paris (1763).

chapters.title: Revolution
chapters.blurb: Royal Proclamation, Pontiac's War, the American Revolution and the second Treaty of Paris.

chapters.title: New republics
chapters.blurb: The early United States, the Louisiana Purchase, the War of 1812, independence movements in New Spain.

chapters.title: Expansion and removal
chapters.blurb: Mexican independence, Indian Removal, Texas, Oregon and the Mexican–American War.

chapters.title: Civil War
chapters.blurb: The Confederate States and the Union.

chapters.title: Confederation and the Plains
chapters.blurb: Reconstruction, Canadian Confederation, the Numbered Treaties and the Plains wars.

wildlife.name: American bison
wildlife.note: Tens of millions on the plains; hunted to a few hundred by 1890.

wildlife.name: North American beaver
wildlife.note: The fur trade's quarry, behind many of the posts and much of the inland exploration.

wildlife.name: Passenger pigeon
wildlife.note: Perhaps once the most numerous bird on Earth; the last wild birds were seen around 1900.
